# Auto-generated result tables

Generated by `experiment.py`; table numbers match `paper.md`. Monte Carlo studies use N=10,000 replications unless a header says otherwise; Study 1 KS adequacy threshold = 0.0136; intervals are 95% Wilson score intervals unless a header says McNemar or bootstrap. Tables 1, 2, 7 and 18 of the paper are editorial and are not reproduced here; Table A1 (Appendix A) is generated from the exact fourth-cumulant weights.

## Table 17: Resampling schemes for Box's $M$ under the null ($\alpha=0.05$, $N=1000$ outer replications, $B=200$ resamples)

| null cell | parametric (pooled normal) | within-group, centred | null-imposed (common covariance) | permutation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MVN p=2,k=2,n=10 | 0.045 | 0.000 | 0.017 | 0.046 |
| MVN p=2,k=2,n=30 | 0.050 | 0.000 | 0.051 | 0.049 |
| lognormal p=2,k=2,n=30 | 0.689 | 0.000 | 0.135 | 0.048 |
| normal vs lognormal, equal cov, n=30 | 0.584 | 0.000 | 0.214 | 0.286 |
| normal vs t5, equal cov, n=30 | 0.150 | 0.000 | 0.083 | 0.069 |

The last two cells have equal covariance but *different* distributions, so exchangeability fails there and permutation is not expected to be valid; they are the cells that discriminate the null-imposed scheme from permutation.

## Table A1: Asymptotic weight decomposition of the Box's $M$ limit (per contrast; multiply each weight by $(1-c)$ for the Bartlett-corrected $M$)

| parent | $p=2$: weights (multiplicity) | $p=3$: weights (multiplicity) | sum, $p=2$ | sum, $p=3$ | equal weights? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| normal | 1 ($\times$3) | 1 ($\times$6) | 3.00 | 6.00 | yes |
| t5 | 5 ($\times$1), 3 ($\times$2) | 6 ($\times$1), 3 ($\times$5) | 11.00 | 21.00 | no |
| lognormal | 56.47 ($\times$2), 1 ($\times$1) | 56.47 ($\times$3), 1 ($\times$3) | 113.94 | 172.40 | no |

For $k$ groups each per-contrast weight is repeated $k-1$ times, so the limit law has $\nu=p(p+1)(k-1)/2$ terms. Under normality all weights equal 1 and the sum is $\nu$; under $t_5$ and lognormal the weights differ, so no scalar multiple of $M$ is $\chi^2_\nu$.
